answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Fingerprinting. Each identity gets a persistent behavioural signature (timing, action mix, graph position) stored in an atlas keyed by epoch. Every new epoch must match the prior signature within a fixed tolerance; a plume of divergent traces flags the cluster for review. Identities that fail consistency forfeit accumulated umber-weighted reputation. Attackers must maintain many costly, coordinated behaviour profiles over time, not just register cheap new keys.
